proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: The maximal open W with G_W to W having P exists with its characterizing properties by Descent, largest-open-of-the-base. The transport morphism G x_{U,t} R to R x_{s,U} G over R, (g, r) mapping to (r, r^{-1} composed with g composed with r), is an isomorphism (its inverse given by the same formula read backwards), so the base changes of G to U along t and along s are isomorphic over R. By the pullback characterization of the maximal open proved in the Descent lemma, the largest open of R over which the base change along t has P equals the largest open over which the base change along s has P; the former is t^{-1}(W) and the latter is s^{-1}(W), whence s^{-1}(W) = t^{-1}(W), i.e. W is R-invariant. (source lines 693-705)

standard_prerequisites.use: States the target notion: W is R-invariant exactly when its inverse images under s and t agree.

standard_prerequisites.name: Largest open of the base on which a tau-locally checked morphism property holds, with its pullback characterization over base changes (Descent chapter, Lemma descent-lemma-largest-open-of-the-base, canonical tag 06QP)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the maximal open W for G_W to W and, applied to the isomorphic base changes of G to U along t and along s, the equality t^{-1}(W) = s^{-1}(W).

core_obligations: The open W exists with its maximality property by descent-lemma-largest-open-of-the-base. Transport step: the morphism G x_{U,t} R to R x_{s,U} G given on points by (g, r) maps to (r, r^{-1} composed with g composed with r) is an isomorphism over R, the composition in the groupoid being denoted by circle; hence the base change of G to U along t : R to U is isomorphic over R to its base change along s : R to U. Conclusion: by the pullback characterization of the maximal open proved in descent-lemma-largest-open-of-the-base, the largest open of R over which the base change along t has P equals the largest open of R over which the base change along s has P; the former is the preimage t^{-1}(W) and the latter is s^{-1}(W). Hence s^{-1}(W) = t^{-1}(W), which by the definition of R-invariant opens means W is R-invariant.
proof_roadmap: Take W and its characterizing maximality from descent-lemma-largest-open-of-the-base (proof lines 694-695).
Write the transport isomorphism G x_{U,t} R to R x_{s,U} G, (g, r) maps to (r, r^{-1} g r), identifying the base changes of G along t and along s (proof lines 696-701).
Apply the pullback characterization of the maximal open to both base changes to get t^{-1}(W) = s^{-1}(W), i.e. R-invariance (proof lines 702-704).
